response.consequence: A user can add blacklisted guests by changing the case of the address. Duplicate attendee rows can be created. Existing attendees and blacklisted addresses receive 'guests added' emails.
response.explanation: The blacklist is lowercased, but each `guest` is compared as typed. `Blocked@x.com` therefore passes `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` when `blocked@x.com` is blacklisted. The same applies to the existing-attendee check `guest === attendee.email`. Duplicates inside the input are also not removed on the server, because that check exists only in the client dialog. `createMany` would insert `a@x.com` twice if a client calls the API directly. Separately, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the raw input rather than `uniqueGuests`. Blacklisted and already-present addresses that were filtered out are still emailed.

other_findings.consequence: One authenticated request with thousands of emails causes heavy DB, CPU and email work. It can also be used to send mass email.
other_findings.explanation: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()`. The handler runs a translation lookup per attendee, an `attendees.some` scan per guest, a `createMany`, and email sending for the whole list. All of this scales with the array size.
